key_facts: Patient is a woman in her 50s
Diagnosed with stage IV B-RAF V600E mutant malignant melanoma
Metastases in liver, lungs, and peritoneum
Developed skin symptoms within 2 weeks of starting ipilimumab
Experienced initial improvement and later disease recurrence
Received a second course of ipilimumab 14 months later
Symptoms recurred and worsened after second course of ipilimumab
Physical findings include photodistributed erythematous to violaceous eruption
Elevated creatine kinase levels (1088 U/L and 1854 U/L)
Antinuclear antibody titer: 1:640 with speckled pattern
MRI showed mild short TI inversion recovery hyperintensity of bilateral vastus lateralis and rectus femoris muscles
Vastus lateralis muscle biopsy showed atrophy of type II muscle fibers

raw.rationale: The patient developed skin symptoms within 2 weeks of starting ipilimumab treatment, and the symptoms recurred and worsened after the second course of ipilimumab, suggesting a temporal relationship between ipilimumab treatment and the development of dermatomyositis

rejected.label: Melanoma-associated dermatomyositis
rejected.why: While the patient has melanoma, the temporal relationship between ipilimumab treatment and symptom development suggests a more direct cause

rejected.label: Paraneoplastic dermatomyositis
rejected.why: Paraneoplastic syndromes are typically associated with the underlying cancer itself, rather than a treatment

rejected.label: Dermatomyositis
rejected.why: This diagnosis is too broad and does not account for the specific temporal relationship with ipilimumab treatment

rejected.label: Polymyositis
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and biopsy results are more consistent with dermatomyositis, which includes skin manifestations
